problem.text: Find the remainder when $9 \times 99 \times 999 \times \cdots \times \underbrace{99\cdots9}_{\text{999 9's}}$ is divided by $1000$.

steps.title: Where to start: every factor is one less than a power of $10$
steps.body: The product is enormous, but a remainder when dividing by $1000$ only depends on the remainder of each factor. The clue is that every factor is a string of $9$s, which is one less than a power of $10$. Once there are at least three $9$s, that power of $10$ is a multiple of $1000$.

your_turn.prompt: What remainder does $9999 = 10000 - 1$ leave when divided by $1000$? What negative number acts the same way?
your_turn.answer: It leaves $999$, which acts like $-1$, because $10000$ is a multiple of $1000$.

steps.title: Count the factors that act like $-1$
steps.body: In the same way, $999$ and every longer string of $9$s act like $-1$ modulo $1000$. Only the first two factors, $9$ and $99$, are smaller than $1000$, so we leave those two as they are. The factors have $1, 2, 3, \dots, 999$ nines, one factor for each length.

your_turn.prompt: How many of the factors have at least three $9$s?
your_turn.answer: All but the first two, so $999 - 2 = 997$ factors.

steps.title: Find the sign
steps.body: So the product leaves the same remainder as $$9 \cdot 99 \cdot (-1)^{997}.$$ A product of $-1$s is $+1$ when there is an even number of them and $-1$ when there is an odd number.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: The product acts like $-9 \cdot 99 = -891$. Careful: a remainder cannot be negative, so add $1000$ to get $-891 + 1000 = 109$. The answer is **$109$**.
